\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عود} (ʿūd)}{عود (ʿūd)}]{\ar{عود} (ʿūd) — an oud, a lute}

\label{lesson:AR-C544-ud}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a composer, then the Arabic for a choir.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عود}}
\textbf{\ar{عود}} — \emph{ʿūd} — \textquotedblleft{}an oud, a lute\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يعزف} \ar{جدي} \ar{على} \ar{العود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaʿzifu jaddī ʿalā al-ʿūd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather plays the oud.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أعواد}, \emph{aʿwād}.

It also means a stick of wood.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عود}} (\emph{ʿūd}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-w-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to return; wood\textquotedblright{} (Lane). The ʿūd is the instrument of wood; English lute goes back to al-ʿūd (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿūd}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿūd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yaʿzifu jaddī ʿalā al-ʿūd.} — My grandfather plays the oud.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a composer, then the Arabic for a choir, then say \emph{ʿūd} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عود} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An oud, a lute\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كمان} (kamān)}{كمان (kamān)}]{\ar{كمان} (kamān) — a violin}

\label{lesson:AR-C544-kaman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a choir, then the Arabic for an oud.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كمان}}
\textbf{\ar{كمان}} — \emph{kamān} — \textquotedblleft{}a violin\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تتعلم} \ar{أختي} \ar{الكمان} \ar{في} \ar{المدرسة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tataʿallamu ukhtī al-kamān fī al-madrasa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister is learning the violin at school.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كمان}} (\emph{kamān}) was borrowed into Arabic and is usually traced to Persian \emph{kamān}, \textquotedblleft{}a bow\textquotedblright{}: the violin is the instrument played with a bow.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kamān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kamān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tataʿallamu ukhtī al-kamān fī al-madrasa.} — My sister is learning the violin at school.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a choir, then the Arabic for an oud, then say \emph{kamān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{طبل} (ṭabl)}{طبل (ṭabl)}]{\ar{طبل} (ṭabl) — a drum}

\label{lesson:AR-C544-tabl}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an oud, then the Arabic for a violin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{طبل}}
\textbf{\ar{طبل}} — \emph{ṭabl} — \textquotedblleft{}a drum\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ضرب} \ar{الولد} \ar{على} \ar{الطبل} \ar{بقوة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḍaraba al-walad ʿalā aṭ-ṭabl bi-quwwa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boy beat hard on the drum.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{طبول}, \emph{ṭubūl}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{طبل}} (\emph{ṭabl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṭ-b-l}, \textquotedblleft{}a drum; to beat a drum\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Ṭabbāl is a drummer.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ناي} (nāy)}{ناي (nāy)}]{\ar{ناي} (nāy) — a reed flute}

\label{lesson:AR-C544-nay}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a violin, then the Arabic for a drum.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ناي}}
\textbf{\ar{ناي}} — \emph{nāy} — \textquotedblleft{}a reed flute\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سمعنا} \ar{صوت} \ar{الناي} \ar{في} \ar{الليل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{samiʿnā ṣawt an-nāy fī al-layl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We heard the sound of the reed flute in the night.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ناي}} (\emph{nāy}) was borrowed from Persian \emph{nāy}, \textquotedblleft{}a pipe, a flute\textquotedblright{}, whose Middle Persian ancestor also meant a reed (EtymDB): the flute is a hollow reed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nāy}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nāy}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samiʿnā ṣawt an-nāy fī al-layl.} — We heard the sound of the reed flute in the night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a violin, then the Arabic for a drum, then say \emph{nāy} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فرقة} (firqa)}{فرقة (firqa)}]{\ar{فرقة} (firqa) — a band, a troupe}

\label{lesson:AR-C544-firqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a drum, then the Arabic for a reed flute.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فرقة}}
\textbf{\ar{فرقة}} — \emph{firqa} — \textquotedblleft{}a band, a troupe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{غنت} \ar{فرقة} \ar{موسيقية} \ar{في} \ar{الحفلة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ghannat firqa mūsīqiyya fī al-ḥafla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A band sang at the party.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{فرق}, \emph{firaq}.

It names any group: \ar{فرقة} \ar{مسرحية}, a theatre troupe.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فرقة}} (\emph{firqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-r-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to separate, to divide\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Farq, a difference, which you know, is from the same root: a firqa is a part set apart.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{firqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghannat firqa mūsīqiyya fī al-ḥafla.} — A band sang at the party.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a drum, then the Arabic for a reed flute, then say \emph{firqa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
